response.consequence: A user can get spurious denials for resources whose name and folder concatenate to the same string as a previously denied pair. Entries live for the short cache TTL.
response.explanation: userPermDenialCacheKey builds the key as namespace.perm_uid_action_name_parent. Name and parent are joined with "_" and are not escaped. Resource names and folder UIDs can contain underscores. A denial cached for (name "a_b", parent "c") produces the same key as one for (name "a", parent "b_c"). Check short-circuits to Allowed:false on any hit in permDenialCache, before it looks at permissions. A user who was denied one resource can therefore be wrongly denied a different resource they are allowed to access, until the cache entry expires. The key also shares the "perm_<uid>_<action>" prefix with the permission-map key, though the trailing fields keep the two apart. The failure direction is deny, not allow, so this is not an authorization bypass.
response.title: Denial cache key joins variable fields with "_", so keys can collide
